messages.subject: stan runs very slowly
parts: I am now doing my master's project. It is a two-parameter logistic item response model.The attachment is my stan code. In the code, I=14405, j=38.K=5 I tried to run for 500 iterations and it took almost two days. Can anyone tell me why it so slow? What should i do to speed the process.

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan runs very slowly
parts:
Hi, some quick comments:
- parameterize in terms of tau, not tau_sq.
- don't use inv-gamma priors
- use stronger priors on alpha, beta, and make sure your problem is roughly on unit scale
- your expression for eta1 needs no loop; just do:  eta1=beta[j1]*(theta[i1]-alpha[j1])
- I don't know what W looks like, but if it has a constant term, you're going to have very weak identification of its coefficient along with the alphas.
- Another source of weak identification is the multiplicative nonidentification of beta with theta,alpha.
It's these last couple of issues that are probably causing the slowness.  Take a look at the section in the Stan manual on item response theory; that should help.

Andrew

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan runs very slowly
parts:
The time the algorithm takes involves two factors:

1. time to evaluate density and gradient

This grows proportional to the data, modulo any issues with
memory throughput and caching.

2. number of density and gradient evaluations per iteration

This grows with the condition of the posterior, roughly
whether or not there are ridges with both flat and
steep components in different directions. Then we need
smaller stepsizes to simulate the Hamiltonian, so we
require more density and gradient evaluations per iteration.

- Bob
